audit_2026_11_02: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-11-02) — DeKalb was the leading Georgia candidate after the 2026-10-31 run: its 'issued collapse' skip that night was RETRACTED the same night (the figures came from a flapping snapshot of this server; the verified ladder showed ~12,920 TTM issued). This audit therefore ran with repeated-read stability checks, per the retraction's own instruction. (1) Layer 'Hansen Building Applications' (DeKalb County GIS, public access): 95,272 rows all-time, issuedDateTime 1988-06-08 to 2026-11-02 (today, at audit time); the layer publishes NO editingInfo stamp, so freshness is the freshest issuedDateTime (see update_cadence). (2) VOLUME STABILITY — the single-bound issued ladder (two-bound TIMESTAMP ranges undercount on this server, verified 2026-10-31; single-bound only): >=2023-01-01: 61,934 / >=2024-01-01: 41,336 / >=2025-01-01: 23,499 / >=2025-11-02: 12,900 / >=2026-01-01: 10,896 / >=2026-09-01: 2,324 / >=2026-10-01: 1,093 — matching the retraction's verified ladder (61,892 / 41,294 / 23,457 / 12,920 at >=2025-10-31 / 10,854 / 1,051) within two days of live growth. Months run 949-1,231 through the whole window — no collapse. (3) STABILITY PASSES: pass 1 (02:01Z) total 95,272, window 12,900; pass 2 (~02:20Z) total 95,272, window 12,901 (+1), issued >=2026-01-01 10,897 (+1), >=2026-10-01 1,094 (+1) — every delta is a single new permit issued that morning, the signature of a live register, not a snapshot flap (which on this server swings thousands). (4) IDENTITY measured on a full audit pull of the window (12,900 rows): the register's grain is one row per permit application plus exact mirror copies — 789 applicationNumbers carry a second (one a third) row, and those groups disagree on NONE of issued/application dates, address, status, work type, occupancy, either valuation field, scope, or district. One published permit = one applicationNumber (12,110 window applications), collapsed in the pipeline. (5) POPULATION: 'Owner Change Only' records (workType D-OWNF, 112 window applications) authorize no work — a change of record — and are excluded at pull (the San Antonio / Pittsburgh family exclusion); the published window is 11,998 permits. (6) COVERAGE: the county's own Hansen permitting system — DeKalb County issues through it for the unincorporated county, and records show it also processing reviews for partner cities (comments name Brookhaven, Clarkston, Stonecrest, Tucker, Doraville permit numbers). Incorporated cities running their own systems are not in this feed. (7) TERMS: the ArcGIS item 'Building Permit Applications' (owner DeKalbGISAdmin, access public) carries no license text of its own; the county's official DeKalb County Permit Tracker for this same system carries a CC BY 4.0 license; figures are published 'as reported by DeKalb County' with attribution, no endorsement implied. Audit evidence: ~/workspace/goals/permitsbycounty/hidden_files/expansion-2026-11-02/.
coverage_note: Permits recorded in DeKalb County's building-permit system (the county's Hansen register). The county issues through this system for unincorporated DeKalb County, and the register also carries the county's permit reviews for several incorporated cities it serves; DeKalb cities that run their own permitting systems are not in this feed, so totals here are DeKalb County system totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one applicationNumber in DeKalb County's Hansen register. The register's grain is one row per permit application plus exact mirror-duplicate rows; a permit's rows are collapsed in the pipeline (registry collapse_events, key = applicationNumber) and represented by the first row in pull order. 'Owner Change Only' records are excluded at pull (registry pull_where_extra) — they are changes of record, not permits authorizing work.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issuedDateTime >= 2025-11-02), measured 2026-11-02 on a full audit pull: 12,900 rows = 12,110 distinct applicationNumber; the 789 multi-row groups disagree on none of the collapse agreement fields (issued/application dates, address, status, work type, occupancy, valuation, scope, district). Excluding the 112 Owner Change Only applications leaves 11,998 published permits (12,783 pulled rows at pass-2 measurement; the pipeline re-measures at build). The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: locationLine1, as published (street address; present on all 12,900 window rows; whitespace collapsed, all-caps values title-cased). City and ZIP are parsed from the free-text location field only when it states them in 'GA <zip>' form (see the normalizer); otherwise they stay NULL — the feed publishes no structured property city/ZIP field. Measured at build: city carried on 555 of 11,999 published permits, ZIP on 564.
field_map.application_date: applicationDateTime (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date). On 230 of 12,110 window permits the source's application timestamp postdates its issue timestamp (a re-issuance artifact in the county's system); mirrored as reported, never adjusted.
field_map.category: The feed's OccupancyTypeDescription is a building occupancy class (Single Family Detached / Business / Apartment / ...), not a permit residential/commercial class — category stays NULL (the Boston treatment).
field_map.contractor_rule: The register publishes NO contractor or business-name field. Its only name-bearing fields are the primaryContact* set (a contact person's name, email, phone, and ids) and applicationName (which carries person surnames, e.g. 'Phillips Residence') — BOTH are excluded from pull_select and never requested from the API at all, so contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the Boston treatment).
field_map.issue_date: issuedDateTime (epoch ms, converted). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the county records an issue date.
field_map.permit_number: applicationNumber (the county's public application/permit number; unique per published permit after the collapse, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: WorkTypeDescription, the county's own work-family naming (New Construction, Residential Air Conditioning, General Combined Plumbing, ...), read together with the workType code for the trade classification — see trades.classify_dekalb_trade: the descriptions name the licensed trades; the mechanical family's two combination codes (M-R+ / M-C+) classify as hvac on sampled scope evidence, Fats Oil Grease (a watershed compliance review) stays general, and Fire Marshal Special Work gets its own fire-marshal trade.
field_map.status: status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Published-window statuses at build: Issued 6,085 / Closed 5,808 / Void 49 / Open 41 / Stop Work 16 — every published record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: declaredValuation FAILED validation on the full window (measured 2026-11-02) and is NOT published: valuation stays NULL and DeKalb publishes counts only. Evidence: the field is the PROJECT's declared value restated across the project's separate permits — $81,845,000 stands on both the new-construction permit and a plumbing permit for 2781 Lulah Ave; $17,453,513 stands on three permits at 1460 Moreland Ave (new construction, electrical, and a temporary-pole permit); $1,843,450 stands on five same-day alteration permits at 1881 2nd Ave. The register's largest figures sit on non-construction permits (a $48,000,000 plumbing permit; $35,000,000 on a Fire Marshal record; $30,225,456 on a Fats Oil Grease record). And 1,070 of 12,110 permits state $1 or less (483 at $0, the rest $0.01-class placeholders). calculatedValuation is populated on only 1,034 permits and is no substitute. No aggregation — raw, per-application, or per-address — is trustworthy (one address hosts many independent projects over time, so no project key exists), so per the Austin/Miami-Dade precedent the pages ship without any dollar figure and the reason is stated on the Data Sources page. The raw declaredValuation stays in pull_select/vault as reported, unpublished, and is re-validated only if the source's field changes character.

history_range: issuedDateTime 1988-06-08 onward in the source (95,272 rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Public access via DeKalb County GIS; the county's Permit Tracker for this system is published under CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International); attribution: DeKalb County, Georgia
order_sql: issuedDateTime ASC, applicationNumber ASC, OBJECTID ASC
rate_limit: ArcGIS county-server query, 2,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily. Note (measured 2026-10-31 and honored in this build): this server undercounts two-bound TIMESTAMP ranges and has served flapping snapshots in the past — audits use single-bound ladders and repeated passes, and gate 4's count-match plus baseline guards every pull.
source_name: DeKalb County GIS — Building Permit Applications (Hansen)
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-02: the ArcGIS item record for 'Building Permit Applications' (publisher: DeKalb County GIS, owner DeKalbGISAdmin; access public) carries no license text of its own and no restriction on reuse; the county's official DeKalb County Permit Tracker — the county's own public window on this same permitting system — is published under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license; figures are published 'as reported by DeKalb County' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Live register (permits issued the same morning were in the feed at audit time). The layer publishes no editingInfo dataset stamp, so freshness (gate 5) is measured as the freshest issuedDateTime in the table under a 96h threshold (the Philadelphia treatment): MEASURED 2026-11-02: max issuedDateTime 2026-11-02T19:31:38Z, the day of the pull.
watermark_field: issuedDateTime + applicationNumber — refresh re-pulls by the issuedDateTime watermark and upserts; the collapse re-runs on every pull, so mirror rows can never double-count.
